protocol.purpose: separate adapter learning-rate matching from explicit gain changes for r8/s12 and r16/s6, then confirm quality against r8/s16
protocol.calibration_metric: mean highest-FP32 fixed-input adapter-delta single-step update RMS across six blocks, steps 50/100/250/500 and seeds 60/61
protocol.selection: closest absolute log(mean update / target); excludes loss, validation, FID and class agreement
protocol.correction: clip(previous multiplier * target / previous update metric, 1/16, 16)
protocol.gain_design: fixed 1/sqrt(r), or (16/s)/sqrt(r) as one empirical width-compensation alternative; same gain throughout each calibration/confirmation recipe

auxiliary_classifier.purpose: fixed auxiliary evaluator of generated requested-class agreement
auxiliary_classifier.retention: one frozen evaluator and its compact training records until explicitly removed

protocol.estimated_new_gpu_hours: 7–10 aggregate including bounded calibration, validation, diagnostics and final evaluations; startup additional
protocol.retention: compact source/configs/seeds/splits/metrics/logs/audits/plots until explicitly removed; no grids, model/evaluator weights or generated datasets
limits: One alternate gain per shape; this is targeted sensitivity, not exhaustive hyperparameter optimization.
Gain times 16/s is an empirical compensation heuristic, not a variance-preservation or muP derivation.
The rate changes every adapter parameter group; gain also changes function scaling. These are different optimization parameterizations.
Matching scalar early update RMS does not match every seed/block, later update, live magnitude or entire-network update.
Calibration seeds 60/61 and confirmation seeds 62/63/64 are independent of previous screens; no quality-based recipe selection.
Default-rate controls keep LR multiplier 1; calibrated gains/rates freeze before any quality run and never retune on quality.
All equal-shape models share base initialization; gain/rate variants of one rank/width share adapter initialization.
r8/s12 and r16/s6 approximately match decoder budget, but encoder/bias totals and training memory differ.
Three training seeds, one held-out split and sampling seed; sample SD is not a confidence interval.
FID uses 5,000 real/generated images and class agreement uses the existing frozen auxiliary classifier.
Concurrent eager training is not an isolated speed or equal-time quality comparison.
Broadcast class/time only; no new ViT/LM, cross-attention, sequence retrieval or structured-operator experiments.

limitations: One fixed validation split; seed spread is not a confidence interval or test-set estimate.
FID uses held-out train images and finite sample counts; not published 50k-image FID.
Wrong-class loss measures sensitivity/use, not generated class accuracy.
External condition is a single class/time vector; sequence-conditioned cross-attention is not evaluated.
Concurrent throughput shares CPU/storage; matrix FLOPs omit non-matmul work and backward.
Generative evaluation time includes sampling and FID feature/statistic computation; isolated inference throughput is not measured.
Each screen has its own declared LR/initialization recipe; optimal rates are not established without bracketing.

limits: One alternate gain per shape; this is targeted sensitivity, not exhaustive hyperparameter optimization.
Gain times 16/s is an empirical compensation heuristic, not a variance-preservation or muP derivation.
The rate changes every adapter parameter group; gain also changes function scaling. These are different optimization parameterizations.
Matching scalar early update RMS does not match every seed/block, later update, live magnitude or entire-network update.
Calibration seeds 60/61 and confirmation seeds 62/63/64 are independent of previous screens; no quality-based recipe selection.
Default-rate controls keep LR multiplier 1; calibrated gains/rates freeze before any quality run and never retune on quality.
All equal-shape models share base initialization; gain/rate variants of one rank/width share adapter initialization.
r8/s12 and r16/s6 approximately match decoder budget, but encoder/bias totals and training memory differ.
Three training seeds, one held-out split and sampling seed; sample SD is not a confidence interval.
FID uses 5,000 real/generated images and class agreement uses the existing frozen auxiliary classifier.
Concurrent eager training is not an isolated speed or equal-time quality comparison.
Broadcast class/time only; no new ViT/LM, cross-attention, sequence retrieval or structured-operator experiments.
